subject: zombie
label: zombie, in the place of the game's models/zombie.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hassassin.mdl, models/barney.mdl, models/scientist.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, A, D, B where the asset was B, D, D, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The silhouette is a hunched, forward-leaning figure with arms out in front, which matches the walk and attack. But the brief's parasite body over the head is only a small green-grey dome on the head (sides.png, FRONT, LEFT, RIGHT), not a large mass over it. The lab coat's hem and sleeves are clean and whole in every side view, with no tears, so the torn coat is not in the outline either.

M2.reason: The brief gives only a height of about 68. The asset measures 62.2 tall, 8.5% under, inside the 15% band for a size the brief gives. Length 39.3 and width 37.1 are not asked for and are not judged.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked down to the small ones: head, parasite body over the head (a major part), lab coat, trousers, shoes, two hands, and about four to five claws per hand. Both hands have their claws, and the shoes and the coat's hip pocket are there. The parasite body is only a small green cap on the head (sides.png, FRONT and TOP), not a body over it, and the coat has no torn edges. That is a major part at the wrong shape, so M3 is at most 1.

M4.reason: The regions are one flat grey-white for the coat and grey-white for the trousers, with no region in the blood-red or brown the brief asks for on the coat. The head is a green-grey that reads as the parasite, which is close. The missing blood is a painted-region difference, so it is charged here and under M5.

M5.reason: The brief's torn and bloodied coat is largely missing. The only wear is the yellow streak on the chest (FRONT-RIGHT) and dark marks on the trousers (BACK, BACK-RIGHT), which do not read as blood. No tears, rips or stains on the coat show in any of the ten views.

M6.reason: Measured by the line-up test, not by this judge. The asset is A in lineup.png. Across the four readings, the judges picked D, A, D, B where the asset sat at B, D, D, B: the asset was caught in 2 of 4, below the three-of-four bar, so it passed as one of the game's.

M7.reason: The front is the front: the figure stands upright, facing the viewer, feet flat on the floor in FRONT and FRONT-LEFT, with its origin at the feet. The forward hunch is the brief's pose, not a fault in facing or placing.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors, and 704 triangles sit under the cap of 1008 (twice the 504 median). But in the attack frames (attack.png 0/7, 2/7, 4/7) the claws look held off the hands, several units out from the wrist, not joined to them. That reads as floating, so M8 is 1. The coat shows no open or inside-out part in the views a player sees.

C1.reason: Through the walk (motion.png) the body, head and arms stay joined and move as a hunched shamble should. In the attack (attack.png), the claws drift away from the hands across several frames, and that comes apart from the body, which C1 does not allow. The walk's claws also hang slightly off the hand in frames 3 and 13.
